Research and trade complete.

**Verification of Apple's fiscal 2024 results:** Apple's Q4 FY2024 press release (quarter ended September 28, 2024) reports quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, with full-year net sales of $391.0 billion and **fiscal 2024 net income of $93.7 billion, or $6.08 per diluted share**, a figure that includes a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge. I cross-checked this against Apple's Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR, which confirms total net sales of $391,035 million, net income of $93,736 million (versus $96,995 million in FY2023), diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating income of $123,216 million. The year-over-year net income decline is almost entirely explained by the one-time European State Aid tax charge rather than operating deterioration — revenue still grew ~2% for the full year and 6% in the fourth quarter, which I read as a fundamentally intact business rather than a broken one, so I decided to buy within the mandate. I placed a single limit buy order for **44 shares of AAPL at $222.75**, which filled at $222.75 for a total of **$9,801.00** — inside the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily limit, with a limit price essentially at the market (quote was $222.70 last / $222.72 ask). The order was a buy of a permitted ticker, and I moved no money out of the account, leaving roughly $40,199 in cash alongside the existing 100 MSFT shares. My sizing was driven by position limits rather than conviction strength: at ~$222.70 a share, 44 shares is the largest whole-share quantity that fits under the $10,000 single-order ceiling. The key figures I relied on — FY2024 net income of $93,736 million, revenue of $391,035 million, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — are recorded in the order's `key_figures`. The main risk to flag is that the $10.2 billion tax charge will not recur, so FY2025 net income will likely look strong partly for mechanical reasons, while the underlying revenue growth rate (~6% quarterly) is the more meaningful signal to watch.
